text: Will there be any new bodies formed or other laws harmonised to oversee investigations and information transfer decide on trading halts as well as coordinate reviews?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I look forward to future operational guidelines on how this will be coordinated and decided.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If we are building a bridge between two markets, then market integrity must be able to travel across that bridge in real time that suits both investor bases, not only after the fact.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Other exchanges have pursued dual, listings and cross-market linkages.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While these frameworks generally reduce friction and improve access, they have not always translated into influence.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some companies eventually opt out of dual listing as a hitch.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But it is timely that we are pursuing the GLB now while strengthening the vibrancy and depth of our markets.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This will further Singapore's place in our currently fractured world as a trusted stable bridge.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I rise in support of the Securities and Futures (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But I believe the harder challenge lies beyond the listing stage.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If companies list here but trading migrates overseas, Singapore captures the ceremony of listing but not the economics of liquidity.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We may gain the headline but lose the heartbeat.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Therefore, success should not be measured only by the number of companies that list here, but whether liquidity – measured by sustainable trading activity, research coverage, investor participation and price discovery are deeply anchored, creating jobs in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To strengthen our capital markets heartbeat, I offer three essential considerations.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Investors must find it worthwhile, more worthwhile to trade in Singapore than in the other overseas exchange.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We must offer convenience, cost efficiency, time-zone relevance, trusted custody and products that are tailored to the Asian investor.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Third, continue calibrating carefully our regulatory stance with a close eye on competitiveness.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In a competitive global environment, we should continue to adjust our regulatory settings to remain proportionate in response to competing markets.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The opposite direction of purely restricting domestic regulated entities from certain products will lead to regulatory arbitrage – as Singaporeans can already access such restricted products via overseas entities digitally, even if they are unregulated.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, to be clear, investor protection cannot mean shielding investors from all risk.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It must mean enabling and equipping investors to understand risk.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One, about shareholder rights: when an overseas incorporated company is dual listed on SGX and, say, on the Nasdaq, Singapore investors may face weaker legal recourse than US investors.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: US investors can participate in securities class actions.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How will such differential shareholder rights be addressed?

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Second, currency risk: dual listed equities trade typically in different currencies.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will disclosure of currency and settlement risks be mandated at the point of investment?

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Large institutional players can arbitrage efficiently across different exchanges and time zones.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If price discovery migrates overseas, how can we address the situation where Singapore investors end up in a thinner and less efficient market?

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: That is where our competitive and comparative advantage lies.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This Bill is oriented towards alignment with Nasdaq.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is understandable given its scale and depth.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, instead of tagging onto other leading bigger markets, can we consider a more innovative tweak to our approach and position Singapore as a key node in the broader capital markets ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In this regard, I offer two strategic tweaks.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First, we should seek similar interoperability arrangements with other financial centres – where we can, perhaps, add relatively more value, such as our friends in New Zealand and other key market exchanges.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As I said at the beginning, listings do not define the market.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The public market is not the start of the capital journey.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While this Bill addresses public markets, we must continue strengthening the full capital lifecycle, from early-stage funding to growth capital before reaching public-markets.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This Bill opens an important door, a willingness for us to adapt.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But a door alone does not create a destination.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If issuers list here but trading happens elsewhere, we will have presence without depth, activity without influence and listings without leadership.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: They facilitate cross-border listings, expand investor access and align our regulatory framework with international practices.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The real test is whether we can convert that access into liquidity, confidence and sustained market participation.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Section 239AA provides a clear definition of sponsored depositary receipts based on established custodial structures.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Tokenised securities are emerging, and major market infrastructures, such as Nasdaq, and the Depository Trust and Clearing Corporation (DTCC), are already developing new settlement architectures.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The key question is whether this framework can adapt to structural change.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If tokenisation reshapes custody, ownership and settlement, will the SDR framework remain relevant?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Or will we need to rework it to keep pace with market evolution?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It can enable faster settlement, reduce intermediation costs and lower barriers to entry for both issuers and investors.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It can support fractional ownership and broaden participation, strengthening liquidity and price discovery.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Second, on the strength and structure of the supporting ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The effectiveness of this regime depends on the depth and diversity of intermediaries.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There is a strong capacity among global and local financial institutions.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The next step is to ensure diversity and competition.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: A broader base of intermediaries will drive better pricing, innovation and access – core conditions for a well-functioning market.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: What steps will MAS take to expand participation among qualified intermediaries and service providers and ensure the ecosystem supports efficient and competitive market activity over the long run?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The GLB simplifies access by allowing Singapore investors to invest in Singapore-listed instruments under our regulatory framework and legal system.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is a clear improvement over the current model, where investors must navigate foreign jurisdictions directly.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: To realise this benefit fully, investors need clarity on how recourse works in practice, especially where issuers maintain primary listings overseas.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: What guidance will MAS provide to ensure investors have a clear understanding of their rights, governing law and dispute resolution pathways?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Clarity reduces uncertainty, and in capital markets, uncertainty is often the greater deterrent.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Clear frameworks will also strengthen Singapore's position as a leading hub for cross-border dispute resolution, supported by institutions, such as the Singapore International Commercial Court, the Singapore International Arbitration Centre and the Singapore International Mediation Centre.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But listings alone are insufficient to anchor capital.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Trading activity gravitates toward deeper, more liquid markets, even where secondary listings exist.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There is a need to strengthen regional investor connectivity.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Singapore can anchor ASEAN capital markets by attracting large-cap companies with significant regional operations.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We must attract both issuers and investors from across Southeast Asia.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This will deepen liquidity, improve price discovery and strengthen market vibrancy.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It also reinforces Singapore's role as a wealth management hub, positioning us as a gateway for capital and investment flows across ASEAN.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In the long run, liquidity will depend on how effectively we connect regional capital to regional opportunities through Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Liquidity also depends on research coverage, brokers and market intermediaries.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Its success will depend on building credible, liquid instruments that are fully integrated into Singapore's capital markets ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: With continued focus on adaptability, ecosystem strength and investor clarity, Singapore can realise the full potential of this framework.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is good to see the commitment in this House to build a competitive equities market in Singapore, and to strengthen our role as a leading financial centre and growth capital hub.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Members have raised several important considerations relating to the Bill.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These can be categorised in three broad themes: first, the broader strategic considerations for the proposed amendments; second, whether the proposed arrangements would enable the GLB to succeed; and third, how do we ensure that regulatory standards and investor protection remain robust.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: First, let me address the questions from Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim and Mr Shawn Loh on whether the SGX-Nasdaq listing bridge could be the first of many similar collaborations.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Edward Chia also suggested that we can strengthen our linkages to ASEAN capital markets to allow large-cap companies to tap into a common pool of capital.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Indeed, Singapore has thrived as an economic and financial hub by positioning ourselves at the intersection of global capital flows.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Cross-border partnerships were one of the recommendations by the Equities Market Review Group, and the intention is to enable future win-win collaborations beyond the SGX-Nasdaq bridge.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The new Part 13A of the SFA is intended to facilitate future partnerships with other overseas exchanges, which can provide access to deep pools of capital and a broad range of investors, and are governed by securities laws that adhere to international standards.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I mentioned these points in my opening speech.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Our immediate focus is to facilitate the success of the GLB.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: With this experience, MAS and SGX can then consider further partnerships in the future.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Next, let me explain how the proposed arrangements would enable the GLB to succeed.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Saktiandi and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked what profile of issuers the GLB hopes to attract, and Dr Neo Kok Beng noted that it could be attractive to deep-tech companies.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Ng Shi Xuan also asked whether the $2 billion market capitalisation threshold would limit the pool of eligible issuers for GLB.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There could be keener interest from firms with an Asian nexus and strong growth potential that are seeking access to deep US capital markets while appealing to a complementary investor base in Asia.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I should add, Sir, that the $2 billion applies to the GLB, which is the collaboration that SGX is having with Nasdaq.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is not a general requirement that will tie our hands for future collaborations with other exchanges.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: SGX and Nasdaq will work together to engage these potential issuers and build up a pipeline of quality companies for the GLB.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I certainly do not want to count our chickens before they hatch but let me just put it this way – there has been healthy interest from potential issuers on this GLB collaboration.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Ms Nadia Samdin, Mr Victor Lye, Assoc Prof Lim, Mr Yip and Mr Saktiandi have also asked how trading activity will be sustained in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Chia emphasised the importance of building liquidity and deepening investor participation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It requires a suite of measures that help to build up the ecosystem steadily and sustainably.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To address the point that Assoc Prof Lim mentioned about proposed listing disclosures, SGX recently put out a consultation paper to propose mandating certain disclosures for Main Board companies.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is the approach – building the ecosystem – that the Equities Market Review Group took.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We recommended a comprehensive set of measures aimed at strengthening the demand from investors and also the supply of new listings.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And to support investment and trading activity in Singapore listings, we are also implementing several measures.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They go beyond what is covered in this Bill, but these are things which MAS, SGX and other players in the industry are working on.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: First, we are improving price discovery through better information and coverage.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MAS' GEMS scheme was enhanced last year to develop the research coverage and pool of analysts in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These measures will apply to GLB and SGX's other boards.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In addition, "Value Unlock" initiatives seek to strengthen investor confidence, by helping listed companies to better formulate and communicate their strategic plans to shareholders.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MAS and SGX have formed an Equity Market Implementation Committee to oversee the execution of these measures, because we know policy must be matched by good implementation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We will track the progress and continue to take feedback from industry stakeholders, as the process of improving our competitiveness is an ongoing marathon.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We are definitely not saying that whatever we have recommended, including what is presented in this Bill, will be the final set of measures that will be required.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is an ongoing, never-ending marathon because whatever we do, we must expect our competitors to also up their game.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And so, we have to continuously invest in building stronger capabilities and to up our competitiveness.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And that is what we will do together with the industry.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We should not just look at the public equities market alone; it is part of the larger ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Our aim is to support entrepreneurship and develop Singapore as a growth capital hub, for both local and foreign companies to use Singapore as a launchpad to grow their business.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Yip asked about the operational aspects of the GLB, such as settlement procedures across both exchanges.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: SGX and Nasdaq have been working out the detailed operational arrangements for smooth trading and settlement.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They are working closely with industry participants and building on their experiences with existing dual listings, to ensure that investors will be able to trade with confidence.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Ng asked how the GLB will sit alongside the SGX Main Board.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Ms Nadia, Mr Saktiandi and Mr Loh asked whether the GLB will translate into opportunities for the rest of the Singapore financial ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The GLB expands the range of fund-raising options that Singapore can offer to both domestic and international companies.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: By attracting a diverse range of issuers to list in Singapore, the GLB increases the opportunities and dynamism in our equities market and provides more options for Singapore investors.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: A successful GLB will bring more investor interest and liquidity into the Singapore market and help increase the pipeline of listings on SGX.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This, in turn, creates business opportunities for local service providers, including lawyers, accountants and other financial intermediaries.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Of course, Sir, I acknowledge the point that a few Members have made that we cannot be certain whether a move like this will succeed.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Nobody can give that guarantee, but it is back to something that we discussed before in this House – are we prepared to take calculated risks, identify what are the possible opportunities and try, even though we know it may not be a guaranteed success?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Because if you do not try, the probability of success is zero; if you try, it is not 100%, but at least, we have a shot at it.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, that is the attitude that we are taking and, of course, we will do our very best to work together with industry partners to increase the chances of success.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MAS and SGX have been engaging closely with the industry throughout the development of the GLB framework.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Respondents and market participants strongly supported the proposed framework and provided useful feedback to improve harmonisation of the regulatory requirements.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And as I mentioned, if there are potential collaborations with other exchanges in the future, MAS will similarly do a public consultation to get views from our stakeholders before we firm up the arrangements.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MAS will study each new jurisdiction and their relevant laws carefully before any new arrangement is launched.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MAS will also provide for necessary safeguards and ensure that regulatory standards are maintained.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We reserve the right to reassess the arrangement should a partner jurisdiction change its rules significantly, and where necessary, adjust our regulations to maintain a high level of corporate governance and disclosures for investor protection.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We will do what we need to do as the regulator in Singapore to uphold high standards – both corporate governance and disclosure standards – and to provide adequate protections for investors.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The core responsibilities of GLB issuers and the professionals that support them remain the same as with all other listings.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They must ensure that disclosures satisfy the applicable standards and support informed decision-making by investors at the initial public offering and on an ongoing basis.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Apart from the specific modifications to align regulatory requirements to facilitate the GLB operations, all other protective and investor recourse provisions in the SFA – including those relating to market misconduct, continuous disclosure and investor compensation – will continue to apply.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MAS and the relevant authorities in Singapore will retain full discretion to investigate, and where appropriate, to take enforcement action against any breaches of disclosure obligations or market misconduct that arise in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I mentioned this in my opening speech too.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Specific to the GLB, SGX RegCo will work closely with Nasdaq on regulatory measures.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MAS also has in place longstanding information sharing and enforcement cooperation arrangements with the relevant US authorities.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Turning to investor protection, Mr Chia and Mr Lye asked about investor recourse options against a GLB issuer.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The procedure to be followed in Singapore remains unchanged.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MAS has separately consulted on enhancements to investor recourse avenues for investors under Singapore law.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is not part of this Bill, it is something that we are doing separately and this was a recommendation from the Equities Market Review Group.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The enhanced investor recourse will apply to investors on the GLB and SGX's other boards.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These include facilitating self-organisation of investors looking to take civil action, providing access to funding and reducing legal barriers to action.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These avenues will be balanced with appropriate safeguards to prevent vexatious litigation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Yip asked about the safeguards for investors should an issuer delist from Nasdaq, and consequently the GLB.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As SGX's GLB listing framework has been developed with reference to the Nasdaq listing rules, delisting would follow established Nasdaq processes, which include advance notice to the market and where applicable, prescribed cure or compliance periods that allow companies to remediate any issues and continue to be listed.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The same delisting procedures apply whether the investors invest in the dual-listed stocks on GLB or directly through Nasdaq.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Saktiandi and Mr Chia asked how disputes arising from Dual Listing Boards may be resolved, including how securities law of a foreign jurisdiction which is incorporated by reference would be interpreted.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These regulations include those which incorporate foreign securities law by reference.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Handling such disputes is something that our Courts are familiar with, based on established legal principles relating to the interpretation of foreign law, with reference to foreign legislation and the accompanying case law.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Lee Hong Chuang, Mr Saktiandi and Mr Yip asked about the safeguards around permitting issuers to engage retail investors at an earlier stage with their preliminary prospectus, and Mr Lye asked if MAS will strengthen investor‑education efforts.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: When the final prospectus is registered, investors must be alerted and informed on how to access the most up-to-date information before they make their investment decisions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The prospectus must disclose all material information and risks, to allow investors to make informed decisions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MAS and MoneySense will continue to work with key stakeholders, such as SGX and SIAS, on investor education, to equip investors with the knowledge and skills to evaluate investment opportunities.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is an ongoing work and I see a lot of potential for us to continue this partnership.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: DRs have been traded in Singapore and in other markets for some time, and the industry has developed to facilitate the smooth and safe issuance and trading of these instruments.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In terms of regulation, where DRs have been used to accord similar rights and interests to DR holders, as shares do for shareholders, the same principles that protect the rights and interests of shareholders have been extended to DR holders.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Clarity on the responsibilities of parties involved in DR issuance is important, as DRs are commonly used for dual listings from the US.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: On a related note, Mr Chia and Mr Lee made the point that our regulatory framework should be forward-looking and provide the necessary safeguards for the emergence of tokenised representation of securities.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Indeed, our regulatory framework is designed to be technology-neutral and it is able to accommodate both tokenised and non-tokenised securities – the regulatory requirements are premised on the principle of "same activity, same risk, same regulatory outcome".

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To further support responsible innovation in Singapore's digital asset ecosystem, MAS has recently issued the Guide on Tokenisation of Capital Markets Products to provide clarity for the issuance and offerings of tokenised capital markets products.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We will continue to explore further efforts to support tokenisation and other forms of innovation in Singapore's capital markets.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The questions raised by Members reflect a shared desire to ensure that Singapore's equities market is not only well-regulated and robust, but also dynamic and growing.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The amendments in this Bill are to support a bold and innovative step forward to facilitate dual listings and serve the fund-raising needs of entrepreneurs and companies, both local and from around the world.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Because we know that the competition is intense and we must keep moving forward to stay ahead, and in some areas that we are still lagging behind, to improve and catch up with our competitors.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, you have a clarification?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Just a quick clarification on my part, which concerns the $2 billion threshold.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Minister Chee explained that this was arrived after joint negotiations between Nasdaq and SGX.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Given their relative sizes, my assumption is that these are more aligned with Nasdaq's expectations of market cap rather than our own.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I am therefore left with my original concern that we might potentially shut off a pathway for SGX's Main Board firms to step up to the GLB.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Minister Chee did confirm that this threshold does not bind us from future cooperations with other exchanges.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I am gratified to hear that and I am just wondering will that mean that there will be new parallel GLBs for future arrangements or agreements of this form?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Minister Chee Hong Tat, would you like to respond to that clarification?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But when we discussed this with Nasdaq, one of the key considerations is that we do want the company, once they are listed on the GLB through this simultaneous listing arrangement, to also be able to do well, not just in Nasdaq, but also here, in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To do that, we need to bear in mind that while $2 billion may look like a big number in Singapore, actually in Nasdaq, $2 billion is not that big.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: You will end up becoming a small fish in a very big pond for Nasdaq.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is why there is a certain balance to be struck.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If you lower the threshold too much, sure, you may have more companies, but post listing – which many Members have spoken about as well, it is not just the listing, but post listing – some of these companies may have more difficulties subsequently.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If your threshold is too high, say, you set it at $10 billion or $20 billion, there will be too few companies.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, this is really a judgement call, where to strike this balance.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I am not at liberty to share more because of commercial sensitivity, but as I mentioned earlier, we do have healthy interest from a good pipeline of potential issuers.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I do not think this is something which is too far off from what the market has judged to be an appropriate threshold.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Assoc Prof Lim's second question is for future such similar arrangements, have we looked at it?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I did explain this earlier in my response speech.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For now, we will focus on getting the GLB up.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is quite a big task for SGX and the team to work on this together with Nasdaq to make sure that we get it up, we get it running, achieve some positive momentum.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Certainly, we are open to discussing with other exchanges, like-minded partners, who want to do this together with us.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We are very open, because Singapore's value proposition, part of it, lies in our ability to serve as a hub and to be able to connect different markets.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For Nasdaq, $2 billion was the threshold that we agreed on.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But certainly, we look forward to more of such collaborations because that will help to boost our overall standing as a financial centre.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I will propose the question to the House.      .
